disease_label_per_paper: TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome with a new pathogenic TNFRSF1A variant in an adult male with renal AA amyloidosis
presentation_summary: Thirty-three-year-old Caucasian man was referred for nephrology consultation because of proteinuria 3.2-5.7 g/day, chronic renal failure with eGFR 69 mL/min/1.73m2, and biopsy-proven kidney AA amyloidosis.
At admission he complained of chronic fatigue; physical examination was otherwise unrevealing except for a post-appendicitis scar.
Laboratory data showed ESR 47 mm/hr, CRP 61.17 mg/L, SAA 60.9 mg/L, negative ANA/ANCA/rheumatoid factor, and negative blood and urine cultures.
Past history revealed recurrent attacks from age 7 with abdominal pain, fever up to 40 C, pharyngitis/tonsillitis, arthralgia of elbows/knees/wrists, and elevated inflammatory parameters.
Attacks recurred irregularly at least twice yearly; fever lasted 7-10 days and abdominal pain 10-14 days. During adolescence acute episodes stopped but chronic low-grade fever and fatigue persisted.
Renal biopsy, TNFRSF1A variant identification, negative MEFV testing, and response to anakinra are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.

actual_treatment.name: colchicine_trial_before_traps_confirmation
actual_treatment.source_text_value: colchicine 0.5 mg twice daily with short-time inflammatory marker improvement; higher dose limited by diarrhea

actual_treatment.name: anakinra_100mg_subcutaneous_daily
actual_treatment.source_text_value: anakinra 100 mg subcutaneously/day as home therapy

outcome.clinical_course: After regular anakinra use, local reactions resolved, fever and fatigue disappeared, CRP/SAA normalized, and kidney function/proteinuria remained stable.
outcome.source_text_value: CRP 0.1 mg/dL and SAA 0.6 mg/dL after treatment; kidney function and proteinuria stable with creatinine 1.7 mg/dL and proteinuria 2.0 g/day.

quality_warnings: Renal biopsy, genetic testing, negative mimic workup, final diagnosis, and treatment response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Proteinuria, inflammatory markers, recurrent prolonged fever history, abdominal pain, pharyngitis, arthralgia, and fatigue are retained as presentation/history evidence.
